problems.title: The stated online positive and negative conditions have overlapping domains
claim: Mathematical transcription, with the surrounding procedure paraphrased: Section 3.3, PDF p. 6, defines the thresholds
The following rule labels a document positive when \(p(d)>T_q^+\), negative when \(p(d)<T_q^-\), and otherwise discards it, without an explicit conflict rule.
analysis: When calibration negatives all lie below positives, \(T^+=\max p_{\rm neg}<T^-=\min p_{\rm pos}\). Any new score \(p\in(T^+,T^-)\) satisfies both \(p>T^+\) and \(p<T^-\), hence both printed label conditions. An explicit overlap rule or branch priority is needed; no observed double-label rate is inferred.

For a two-token gold answer \((a,b)\), let each required conditional probability be \(r\) versus alternative \(1-r\), followed by certain end-of-sequence. Fifty calibration documents with \(r=0.1\) fail greedy exact match and have gold probability \(0.01\); fifty with \(r=0.9\) succeed with probability \(0.81\). Both pools are nonempty. A later document with \(r=0.6\) has gold probability \(0.36\), strictly inside the overlap and satisfies both predicates.
result: A normalized autoregressive example proves ambiguous membership; unavailable training code leaves actual priority and double-insertion incidence unknown.
repair: Explicitly state branch priority, or use the proposed conservative rule: positive above \(\max(T_q^+,T_q^-)\), negative below \(\min(T_q^+,T_q^-)\), and abstain otherwise. The latter is logically disjoint but has untested learning behavior.
problems.impact_rationale: A normalized autoregressive example proves ambiguous membership; unavailable training code leaves actual priority and double-insertion incidence unknown.

problems.title: The re-indexing comparison changes both retrieval representation and indexing strategy
problems.source_location: Section 5.1, Figure 5, PDF p. 10; Appendix H, PDF pp. 22–23.
claim: Paraphrase: Section 5.1, PDF p. 10, interprets the comparison in Figure 5 as favoring late-parametric retrieval over periodic re-indexing. Appendix H, pp. 22–23, gives the detailed setup and attributes the weaker re-indexed configuration to index staleness.

The Appendix H baseline description uses SIDR for the late-parametric system and DPR for the periodic-re-indexing system. It states that the dimensionalities are \(30522\) and \(768\) respectively and explains the change by available GPU memory. The following training description nevertheless characterizes the models as differing only in their in-training retrieval strategies.
analysis: The observed comparison is \(Y(\mathrm{SIDR},\mathrm{late})-Y(\mathrm{DPR},\mathrm{periodic})\). Adding and subtracting \(Y(\mathrm{SIDR},\mathrm{periodic})\) separates a strategy effect from an unmeasured representation effect. The appendix discloses dimensions \(30522\) and \(768\), so this is documented confounding, not concealment. The two-system comparison cannot identify the sign or size of the strategy-only effect.
result: The disclosed backbone change leaves an unmeasured architecture component in the comparison; the complete-system advantage can remain valid.
repair: Restrict the conclusion to the compared complete systems, or use a matched retriever/checkpoint and vary only the refresh policy to identify its effect.
problems.impact_rationale: The disclosed backbone change leaves an unmeasured architecture component in the comparison; the complete-system advantage can remain valid.
